positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described a traumatic event where they felt genuinely threatened and unsafe. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports 'sudden memories or feelings' that disrupt their day, occurring several times a week. Criterion B2 (flashbacks): MET — patient states they replay the event in their mind and feel as if they are back in that moment, which is distressing. Criterion C1 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient consistently tries to avoid thoughts related to the event. Criterion C2 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids certain places and activities that remind them of the trauma. Criterion D1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient experiences difficulty recalling specific details of the trauma. Criterion D2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient expresses overwhelming negativity about themselves and the world. Criterion D3 (blame): MET — patient acknowledges unreasonable self-blame regarding the trauma. Criterion D4 (negative emotions): MET — patient reports feelings of fear and guilt triggered by reminders. Criterion D5 (anhedonia): MET — patient has lost interest in activities they previously enjoyed. Criterion D6 (detachment): MET — patient feels disconnected from others. Criterion D7 (inability to experience positive emotions): MET — patient finds it difficult to engage in happiness. Criterion D8 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability and outbursts. Criterion D9 (recklessness): NOT MET — patient mentions occasional reckless behavior but does not indicate it is consistent. Criterion D10 (hypervigilance): MET — patient feels more on edge and scans their environment. Criterion D11 (startle response): MET — patient reports increased startle response. Criterion D12 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient has difficulty concentrating, especially when reminded of the trauma. Criterion D13 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient experiences difficulty sleeping due to racing thoughts. Criterion E (duration): MET — symptoms began after the traumatic event and have lasted for over a month. Criterion F (functional impairment): MET — patient reports significant distress and interference with work and social interactions. Criterion G (exclusion): NOT MET — patient denies substance use or withdrawal. Total: 12 of 14 criteria met (threshold ≥ 5). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
